note: Real findspot: the Muisca Raft was discovered here in 1969 by local farmers, placed inside a ceramic pot within a cave near Lázaro Fonte.

note: Real findspot: the Siecha Raft was recovered here in 1856 by the Tovar brothers, who were draining the lake in search of gold.

note: Real region associated with Quimbaya burial mound finds, central Cauca River valley, Colombia.

name: Lake Guatavita, Cundinamarca, Colombia

name: Yonaguni Island, Ryukyu Islands, Japan
note: Site of the disputed Yonaguni Monument formation, most-cited pop-culture 'evidence' for Lemuria/Mu.

name: Sunda Shelf, Java Sea
note: Real submerged Ice Age landmass; strongest genuine geological basis for a drowned Southeast Asian homeland.

name: Trinil, Solo River, Java, Indonesia
note: Findspot of the real Java Man (Homo erectus) fossils, later misattributed to Lemuria in pop culture.

name: Gulf of Khambhat, Gujarat, India
note: Site of the disputed 2001 sonar survey claims of a submerged pre-Harappan city.

name: Tashilhunpo Monastery, Shigatse, Tibet
note: Seat of the Panchen Lamas, traditional source of Shambhala guidebook texts including the Shambhala Lanyig.

name: Roerich Expedition Route (Central Asia)
note: Approximate path of the real 1924-1928 Roerich expedition through Xinjiang, Altai, Mongolia, and Tibet in search of Shambhala.

name: Xiaohe Cemetery, Tarim Basin, Xinjiang, China
note: Real findspot of the Tarim Basin mummies, Bronze Age Xiaohe culture.

name: Shetland Islands, UK
note: Leading candidate for Pytheas's Thule; identified by Agricola's Roman fleet and later adopted by Ptolemy.

name: Iceland
note: Leading modern scholarly candidate for Thule (Cunliffe and others), based on six days' sail and hours-of-daylight descriptions.

name: Smola, Norway
note: Modern Norwegian candidate site actively promoting its claim to the Thule identification.

name: Thule (Pituffik), Greenland
note: Site of the historic Thule trading post that gave its name to the unrelated Thule archaeological culture.
